1: In Moab, Naomi loses her husband and both sons. Returning to Bethlehem, she urges her daughters-in-law to stay behind. Ruth refuses: "Your people shall be my people, and your God my God."
A foreign woman chooses Israel's God out of faithful love.
2: Ruth gathers leftover grain in a field belonging to Boaz, a relative of Naomi. He notices her loyalty and protects and provides for her.
God's care arrives through the kindness of a good man and the law of gleaning.
3: On Naomi's advice Ruth goes to Boaz at night and asks him to act as her family redeemer. He praises her and promises to settle the matter.
Boaz acts with honour and restraint.
4: At the town gate a closer relative gives up his right. Boaz marries Ruth, and their son Obed becomes the grandfather of King David.
A Moabite widow becomes an ancestor of David and of Jesus. Boaz the redeemer is a figure of Christ.
